rubric.role_summary: Senior aerospace procurement and category-management role shaping suppliers and commercial agreements for an aircraft programme moving through development, certification and industrialisation.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Senior aerospace procurement and category-management role shaping suppliers and commercial agreements for an aircraft programme moving through development, certification and industrialisation.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- Significant procurement/category management experience within aerospace.
- Expertise in at least one of airframe, propellers, powertrain and energy storage, or mechanical systems.
- Experience with long aerospace development cycles, extended supplier lead times and complex qualification/certification requirements.
- Experience negotiating commercial agreements with aerospace suppliers.
- Degree-level qualification in a relevant discipline and/or relevant CIPS qualification.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Experience across complex aircraft or aerospace product-development programmes is ideal.
- Deep understanding of the aerospace product lifecycle, including development, design maturity, qualification, certification, industrialisation and production ramp-up.
- Understanding of global aerospace supply chains and strategic-supplier capability, capacity, financial and operational risks.
- Experience leading complex, high-value negotiations and commercial agreements with aerospace suppliers.
- Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Programme, Certification and Operations teams.
- Experience developing strategic supplier relationships rather than only managing transactional procurement.
- Experience managing suppliers through change, development challenges and evolving product requirements.
- Experience managing suppliers and stakeholders across different markets and cultures.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): Greater Bristol area. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them. Onsite work is based in one of these areas.
